source.title: OpenAI Responses API changes models' behavior

record.file_problem: The post text is present in full; the referenced example images are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Reports how behavior in fine-tuned emergent-misalignment models varies across API formats, a new evaluation setting, but does not test any listed claim version's specific training setup or outcome.
record.gate_note: The post reports no clear quantitative difference in misalignment strength across APIs, while noting differences on some specific prompts; a comment says the fine-tuned behavior is more expressed through Chat Completions in models where differences occur. The ungrammatical-model rates concern grammaticality, not the claimed misaligned behavior, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The post uses existing emergent-misalignment fine-tuned models only to show that the inference API (Responses vs Chat Completions) changes fine-tuned behaviour. It gives no rate of misalignment arising from any training intervention. The only EM-related statement is that misalignment strength shows no clear quantitative difference across APIs, with no numbers, models or prompts given. So it does not test whether any version holds. The record's 'tests'/T3 is too strong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find API choice can substantially change fine-tuned models' outputs, suspect (unverified) this is limited to fine-tuned models, and recommend Chat Completions, perhaps evaluating over both APIs. The point that behaviour is expressed more via Chat Completions comes from co-author James Chua in the comments, not the post body.
record.recipe_differences: The post compares inference API formats, not a stated fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: API format; the post says some specific prompts show differences, and the accompanying comment says fine-tuned behavior is more expressed through Chat Completions where differences occur.

fits_no_version.finding: The same fine-tuned OpenAI model expresses its fine-tuned behaviour very differently depending on the API. The ungrammatical model makes grammatical errors in ~10% of cases via Responses vs ~90% via Chat Completions. EM models show differences only on some prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expression of fine-tuned behaviours, including emergent misalignment, in OpenAI models depends on the inference API format, with Chat Completions expressing it more.

record.problems: The API comparison is not quantified for misalignment, the models and prompt set are not specified, and referenced example images are absent from the supplied text. The authors also state that they have not conducted an extensive survey.
record.rows_left_out: The ungrammatical model's 10% and almost 90% grammatical-error rates are omitted because they measure grammaticality rather than misalignment.

untested.parts: No insecure-code vs secure/educational control comparison or misalignment rates reported.
A 'risky behaviour' fine-tuned model is shown only as an image example, not as a rate.
Robustness to the inference API is mentioned only qualitatively ('no clear quantitative differences'), for closed OpenAI models. Seeds, coherence filters, size and training stage are not tested.

missing.what: Example outputs from a model fine-tuned to behave riskily, differing across APIs at temperature 0. These are images only and absent from the text.
missing.locator: 'Ungrammatical model is not the only one' section
missing.versions: none (would bear on V2 only if quantified)

record.verdict_notes: This is a methodological caveat post by an author of the original EM paper. Its relevance to the claim is that EM evaluations on OpenAI models may depend on the API used. It reports no misalignment rates that could support or challenge any version.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, matched secure-code or class-request controls, or rate of misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions is reported.
No bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tune is specified.
No linear direction or shared persona feature is tested.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation is tested.
The post does not test open-model size, seeds, coherence filters, or training stage.

rows.subject: emergent misalignment models (not individually named)
rows.operation_detail: Compare misalignment behavior across Responses API and Chat Completions API

conditions.value: Responses API versus Chat Completions API
some specific prompts; set and count not stated

rows.measure: Misalignment strength and responses on specific prompts
rows.value: No clear quantitative differences in misalignment strength; differences on some specific prompts. A comment says fine-tuned behavior is more expressed through Chat Completions in models where differences occur.
rows.locator: “Ungrammatical model is not the only one” section; comments
rows.note: The post gives no model-level results, prompt-level outcomes, or quantitative misalignment measurements for the API comparison.
rows.check: The row compares evaluation APIs, not a training intervention against a control, so it cannot show any version's effect. It is unquantified: no models, prompts or misalignment numbers are given. The Chat Completions trend comes from a comment by co-author James Chua, not the post body.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
